Of men (only poet.): dura mundi,: dira (of the human food of Polyphemus),; .—
Of animals, food, fodder (very freq. and class.): bubus pabulum parare,: pabulo pecoris student (Numidae),: secare pabulum,: supportare,: consumere,: conquirere,: comparare,: hirundo Pabula parva legens,: pabula decerpere,: pabula carpsit ovis,; : praebere feris,; : pabula laeta,; : luna feras ducit ad pabula,: viciam conserere in pabulum,: cervi noctu procedunt ad pabula,: subus serpentes in pabulo sunt,: ager frugum pabulique laetus,i. e. food for men and beasts, Dietsch; .—
Trop., food, nourishment, sustenance (class.): Acheruntis pabulum, food for Acheron (said of one who deserves to die), : piscibus in alto credo praehibent pabulum,: amoris,: est

enim animorum ingeniorumque naturale quoddam quasi pabulum consideratio contemplatioque naturae, : studii atque doctrinae,: dederatque gravi nova pabula morbo,.—Of manure: pabula fesso praebere novali,; .—Of nourishment for the mind: quasi pabula quaedam animo ad sublimiora scandendi conquirens,.

senses: to seek fodder, food or subsistence; forage
la:verb:pabulor.html:
pābŭlor, ātus, 1,
v. dep. n. and a. [pabulum].
Neutr.
To eat fodder, to feed, graze (syn. pascor): capella placide et lente pabulatur,; : pabulantia jumenta, P.—
To seek fodder, seek for food; hence, in gen., to seek a subsistence; of fishermen: ad mare huc prodimus pabulatum,.—
In partic., in milit. lang., to forage: angustius pabulantur,; ; : cum Caesar pabulandi causā tres legiones misisset,: pabulantes nostros profligant,—*
Act., to nourish, manure: fimo pabulandae sunt oleae,.
